Migration scoped to `business_author_brand_id IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_typeof(opening_hours)='array'` (zero Google rows touched, idempotent). **Close actions:** merge → deploy `discover-cards` + `run-business-place-authoring-pipeline` + `generate-curated-experiences` from main → iPhone 17 Pro sim acceptance (Lantern renders on Drinks deck during open hours with real photo). Invariant `I-BUSINESS-HOURS-NORMALIZED-TO-GOOGLE-SHAPE`. SPEC: `Mingla_Artifacts/specs/SPEC_ORCH-1068_BUSINESS_VENUES_RENDER_ON_DECK.md`.

> **2026-06-03 — ORCH-1068 [business-authored venues render on the consumer deck] REGISTERED (SPEC ready).** S1-high / `bug` + `architecture-flaw` + `data-integrity`. The raw RPC `query_servable_places_by_signal` has NO hours predicate (proven via `pg_get_functiondef`) so it returns the row — which is why it "looked surfaced" in DB probes but never rendered. **Live proof:** Lantern & Vine `place_pool 8b720912-…` — `is_servable=true`, `deck_eligible`, `drinks` score **200**, `signal_serving_drinks_pct=100` (cohort includes everyone — DISPROVEN as the cause), `opening_hours` is array-shaped, dropped at `filterByDateTime`. **Format-gap inventory (7):** (1) hours-array-vs-object = **GAP, primary blocker**; (2) weekday 0=Mon vs Google day 0=Sun = **GAP, latent off-by-one** (masked because Lantern is open all 7 days); (3) `opening_hours.openNow` absent → curated/person-hero `isOpenNow` = **GAP**; (4) `utc_offset_minutes` NULL → today-mode uses longitude fallback = **GAP, accuracy-only not blocker**; (7) RPC hours-filter = **NO GAP** (correctly absent). **Chosen fix = NORMALIZE-AT-WRITE + BACKFILL (operator's lean) + defensive reader safety-net + image-hero picker.** Rationale: the array leaks into ≥4 consumer readers (discover-cards, generate-curated-experiences openNow, personHeroCards, signalRankFetch/stopAlternatives) all of which already correctly read the Google object — normalizing fixes the whole class at once; teach-the-filter-only would leave the rest wrong. **Plan:** new shared converter `_shared/businessHoursToGoogle.ts` (`day=(weekday+1)%7`, openNow=null, overnight-safe); normalize at both pipeline write sites; **backfill migration `20260905000000_orch_1068_normalize_business_hours.sql`** (remote max `20260904000000`, > all sibling worktrees — free; scoped to `business_author_brand_id IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_typeof(opening_hours)='array'`, idempotent, converts the **3** existing rows [2 servable + 1 processing]); defensive array branch in `discover-cards` + `_shared/curatedStopHours.ts`; hero = first non-video url. **Redeploy from main at CLOSE:** `discover-cards`, `run-business-place-authoring-pipeline`, `generate-curated-experiences`. **C7 allowlist (COMMS-0002):** `ORCH_1068_BACKEND_ALLOWLIST` (migration + converter + test) in `orch-0863-marketing-hub-phase-b.mjs` SAME commit. **Acked COMMS-0018** (build additively on reconciled pipeline source, don't diverge WS7/scorer). **New invariants:** I-1068-BUSINESS-HOURS-CANONICAL-GOOGLE-SHAPE, I-1068-DECK-HERO-IS-IMAGE. **Success gate (SC-ACCEPT):** Lantern & Vine renders on the Drinks deck in Raleigh during open hours with its real photo hero — provable on iPhone 17 Pro sim + Android emu. **Open Qs (non-blocking, recommended defaults given):** OQ-1 leave `utc_offset_minutes` to longitude fallback (no tz API this ORCH); OQ-2 image-hero now, deck cover-video player a future ORCH. **Discovery D-2:** ORCH-1067's "confirm it surfaces on the deck" close action was never deliverable by 1067 alone — THIS open-hours gate is the second independent blocker. > **2026-06-03 — ORCH-1067 [bouncer accepts business-authored uploaded photos] REGISTERED (SPEC ready).** S1-high / `bug` + `architecture-flaw` + `data-integrity`. Builds on META-ORCH-1062 / META-ORCH-1009 Sub-E/F. **Affected Surfaces:** backend (edge-fn logic only — `supabase/functions/`); outcome surfaces Consumer iOS/Android (deck eligibility) + Admin Web (approve outcome). NOT in scope: buyer-web, business-app UI, any DB schema. **Root cause (proven, live DB + full caller trace):** the deck "bouncer" rule **B7** (`B7:no_google_photos`) in `_shared/bouncer.ts:335-338` requires a non-empty Google `photos` array UNIVERSALLY. A business-authored venue is not on Google → empty `photos` → B7 fires even though it has real uploaded photos in `stored_photo_urls`. At admin approval (`admin-review-venue-claim/runApproveGoLive`, a raw `bounce(ppRow)` over a `BOUNCER_SELECT` projection) B7 rejects it, `is_servable` stays false → EVERY business-authored/claimed venue is permanently blocked from the consumer deck. **Live proof:** place_pool `8b720912-…` "Lantern & Vine" — `fetched_via='business_authored'`, `google_photo_count=0`, `stored_photo_count=7`, website+hours present, **`bouncer_reason='B7:no_google_photos'` (single reason)**, `is_servable=false`. All 3 `business_authored` rows have `google_place_id IS NULL` + 0 Google photos; all 80,399 Google-sourced rows have `google_place_id` set + ~100% Google photos (clean partition). **Fix (SPEC ready):** add `fetched_via` to `PlaceRow`; in `bounce()` skip the B7 push when `fetched_via='business_authored'` (B8 stored-photo gate still applies, so a business-authored venue with NO stored photos still fails); add `fetched_via` to the SELECT in the THREE callers missing it (`run-bouncer`, `run-pre-photo-bouncer`, `admin-review-venue-claim`) + to the `placeForBouncer` return in `run-business-place-authoring-pipeline` (4th caller; its 3 sites already swap photos at caller level — fix makes that redundant). **`bounce()` call-site census (exactly 4, proven):** run-bouncer, run-pre-photo-bouncer, admin-review-venue-claim, run-business-place-authoring-pipeline (×3 sites). `claim-search-pool` / `backfill-place-photos` / `run-signal-scorer` reference "bouncer" in comments/columns ONLY — not callers. **Two-pass parity (I-TWO-PASS-BOUNCER-RULE-PARITY):** PRESERVED — the skip is photo-pass-INDEPENDENT (function of `fetched_via`, not `skipStoredPhotoCheck`) so it fires identically in pre-photo + final; B8 remains the only cross-pass difference. Business-authored rows generally bypass the two-pass cycle (all 3 have `passes_pre_photo_check=NULL`) but the runners scan by city without a `fetched_via` filter, so both runners' SELECTs get `fetched_via` for consistency. **No DB migration; no new backend source file** (test files may be added → ORCH-0863 C7 allowlist only if NEW files). **Redeploy ALL 4 callers** (shared `bouncer.ts` dependency). **Predicate locked:** `fetched_via='business_authored'` (narrowest correct — NOT `google_place_id IS NULL`). **New invariant proposed:** I-BOUNCER-B7-SKIPS-BUSINESS-AUTHORED. **Acked COMMS-0018** (same Lantern/Lumen approval-side scorer/photo bug class; complementary — 1067 fixes the photo gate, 1062 fixed the scorer). **Pipeline:** backend ORCH (no designer) → IMPLEMENT (Claude `mingla-implementor`) → TEST (deno bouncer/pipeline/admin-review fails-on-revert) → orchestrator CLOSE (edge-fn deploy owned by orchestrator). Investigation: `Mingla_Artifacts/reports/INVESTIGATION_ORCH-1067_BOUNCER_ACCEPTS_UPLOADED_PHOTOS.md`; SPEC: `Mingla_Artifacts/specs/SPEC_ORCH-1067_BOUNCER_ACCEPTS_UPLOADED_PHOTOS.md`. **Worktree:** `~/Desktop/mingla-orchs/ORCH-1067-[bouncer-accepts-uploaded-photos]/` on branch `ORCH-1067-bouncer-accepts-uploaded-photos`. **Status:** REGISTERED — SPEC ready, awaiting IMPLEMENT dispatch.

> **2026-06-02 — ORCH-1043 [Photo-thumbnail pipeline: server-driven + parallel + scoped + collage fallback] CLOSED PASS — Grade A.** S1-high / `bug` + `performance` + `architecture-flaw`. **Renumbered from ORCH-1033** at close (ID collision: the currency-display ORCH owns 1033 on main per the COMMS-0004 SOP; this orchestrator's anchor was stale at spawn, so the spawn-time scan missed the currency INTAKE). **Affected Surfaces:** backend (`supabase/functions/backfill-place-photo-thumbs`, `supabase/functions/_shared/imageCollage.ts`, migration `20260815000000_orch_1043_thumb_backfill_cron.sql`) + admin-web (`mingla-admin` Thumbnails tab). NOT in scope: consumer iOS/Android, business iOS/Android, buyer-web (the intelligence collage is the ONLY runtime reader of `_thumb.jpg`). **Operator report (Seth):** intelligence runs failing en masse ("✗75/✓33" on London) + the thumbnail backfill itself dying with "Batch failed — not enough compute resources." **Root cause (live-proven):** (1) the collage consumer only fell back off the pre-generated `_thumb.jpg` on HTTP `404`, but a missing thumbnail object returns **HTTP 400** with a `{"statusCode":"404",...}` body — so the fallback never fired → "0 of N photos could be decoded" → place fails. London had 7,234/10,706 servable places (68%) missing thumbnails, matching the ~69% intel-run failure rate. (2) The thumbnail backfill decoded **full-size originals** in-function at batch=25 (~125 decodes/invocation) → edge WORKER_LIMIT 546; and it was **browser-driven** (ran only while the operator's PC + tab stayed on). **What shipped:** (A) `backfill-place-photo-thumbs` converted to a **server-driven** self-invoking `process_chunk` budget loop (`EdgeRuntime.waitUntil`) + new pg_cron `kick_pending_thumb_backfill` (`*/10`), mirroring `tg_kick_pending_trial_runs`; (B) **parallel-N=6** photo-level semaphore with the 800px-cap memory math (6×≤6.4 MB ≈ 38 MB ≪ cap) — no more 546; (C) scoped to `is_servable=true` + has-photos + no-thumb, optional `city` param (targets London's 7,234); (D) the 10-min cron **auto-drains new seeds**; (E) admin Thumbnails tab is now a **status-viewer** over the server run (same UX/controls/cards + optional city dropdown, no browser engine); (F) collage falls back to the **ORIGINAL full-size object** (baseline, decodable) on ANY non-OK thumb response — NEVER the metered render endpoint (ORCH-0957 gate green), with fetch-vs-decode error clarity. **Step 0.5 SATISFIED:** implementor happy-path `imageCollage.fallback400.test.ts` (T-01, fails-on-revert proven at `b6bb54ffe`) + tester adversarial `imageCollage.thumbFallback.test.ts` T-04 + migration test `orch_1043_thumb_backfill_cron.test.ts`. any draft field not registered in one of these Sets gets dropped without warning. **The specific event-date bug is mechanistically distinct from F-A** (it's NOT an unregistered key — `ORCH_0877_WHEN_PATCH_KEYS` already includes `date`), so the investigation must distinguish 3 hypotheses: (H1) the date-picker UI doesn't fire `setPatch({date: ...})` on change, leaving `patch.date === undefined` and the save handler falling through to existing date at `EditPublishedScreen.tsx:789`; (H2) the `business_patch_event_when` RPC has a buyer-protection guard that silently no-ops the date change (docstring at `businessEvents.ts:818-820` says "Time-only edits always succeed regardless of sold count" + "server rejects whenMode/recurrence/multi-date structural changes when sold>0" — `date` is in neither group, possibly falling into a silent-reject gap); (H3) RPC writes to DB correctly + `invalidateServerEventCaches()` fires at line 820 but the Edit screen's local state doesn't refresh from the new cache so user sees stale data even though DB is updated. **Class-of-bug audit scope (audit + report missing fields, do NOT fix all in same PR):** (A) all 5 patch-key Sets in `EditPublishedScreen.tsx` vs the full `EditableLiveEventFields` interface — any field in the interface NOT in any Set is potentially silently un-savable; (D) `marketingCampaignService.ts` + `marketingTemplateService.ts` for the same pattern. **Structural prevention (SPEC must decide):** options include (i) refactor diff builders to use `Object.keys(draft)` so adding a new field is automatic, (ii) add a strict-grep CI gate `silent-save-no-key-drift` that enforces: every field in `EditableLiveEventFields` and `Brand` interfaces MUST appear in the corresponding patch-key Set or diff function, (iii) add a runtime dev-only warning when a draft has keys outside the registered Sets. **Pipeline:** Claude `mingla-forensics` INVESTIGATE — start with the 3 hypotheses above via live-fire repro on business iOS sim (the build operator already has installed) → SPEC the class-wide fix + the prevention CI gate → Codex `implementor-mingla` IMPLEMENT → Claude `mingla-tester` TEST (verify date persists end-to-end on iOS sim + Android emu + the audit-found missing-field cases) → CLOSE. **Queued behind ORCH-0964** close (no code-path overlap; NOT in scope: business iOS/Android native, consumer iOS/Android native (these aren't web), admin-web (desktop-only), buyer-anonymous web on desktop viewports (proven working). **Symptom:** under Playwright `devices["iPhone 13"]` (`hasTouch:true, isMobile:true, viewport:390×844, deviceScaleFactor:3`), buyer-anonymous web routes never reach a stable paint — `page.goto({waitUntil:"load"})` eventually returns and OneSignal env-missing console warning fires (proving bundle init runs) but `page.screenshot()` and `page.getByRole(...)` then hang until test timeout at 60 s. Desktop Chromium + desktop WebKit render the same routes correctly within 5 s. **Discovery context:** surfaced by ORCH-0961 retest (`QA_ORCH-0961_PUBLIC_PAGE_CLOSE_NAV_PARITY_RETEST.md` §6 DISCOVERY-RETEST-1) when testID handles for the new Close+Share IconChrome were not findable in Playwright iPhone-13 simulation. Adding the handles proved the issue is NOT selector resolution — the page itself never mounts to a stable DOM. The same failure was observed in the prior ORCH-0961 v1 QA on commit `d243050b1` (before the rework), confirming the bug pre-dates ORCH-0961's close-button work. **Root-cause hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):** (1) `react-native-reanimated` initialization stalls under WebKit's touch profile — `IconChrome` and other RN components use `useAnimatedStyle` and may need a different bridge path on mobile-touch web; (2) Expo Router's web entry detects touch device and mounts a mobile-only code path that hits an infinite render or unhandled rejection; (3) a paint-stable issue in `@mingla/event-rendering`, `react-native-safe-area-context` web build, or another shared mobile-touch web dependency. **Pipeline (proposed):** Claude `mingla-forensics` INVESTIGATE — priority 1: confirm repro on REAL iPhone Safari + REAL Android Chrome (Playwright simulation is suggestive, not authoritative; if real devices don't repro, the entire ORCH downgrades or closes as "Playwright-iPhone-13-device-profile only — not a user-facing bug"); priority 2: bisect against last known-good buyer-web mobile commit; priority 3: identify the stalling render path with `page.evaluate(performance.getEntries)` + `page.tracing.start`/`stop` traces. Then SPEC → IMPLEMENT → TEST → CLOSE. **Severity rationale:** S1-high because real iPhone Safari buyers may be affected; if confirmed on real devices, this is a production-blocker far broader than ORCH-0961's dead-end fix. If priority-1 INVESTIGATE shows real devices work fine, downgrade to S3-low (Playwright-environment-only artifact). **No worktree spawned yet** — operator decision required: open the investigation now or queue behind ORCH-0963/0964/0965. > **2026-05-22 — ORCH-0921 [Trip payment-plan finalize silently drops `installment_plan_root` + child installments — €375/order revenue leak] REGISTERED — INTAKE.** [SUPERSEDED by CLOSED CONDITIONAL PASS entry above] **S0-critical** (revenue integrity + customer-trust impact). Classification: `bug` + `data-integrity` + `revenue-risk` + `architecture-flaw`. **Plain English:** when a buyer chooses a payment-plan tier at trip checkout, Stripe charges the deposit successfully, the order is created at deposit amount (€125 of €500), but the finalize step that should (a) flip `orders.installment_plan_root` to `true` and (b) INSERT child rows into `order_installments` from the session's persisted `installment_schedule` does NOT run (or runs as a silent no-op). Result: the order shows "Paid in full" against its deposit-only total on the ORCH-0914 Money tab, the `process-scheduled-installments` cron never sees the future installments, the saved PaymentMethod is never charged off-session, and the remaining €375 silently disappears. Until proven otherwise this is the DEFAULT failure mode for every trip booking on a payment-plan tier. **Proof (DB-probe verified 2026-05-22 by orchestrator):** The DC Adventure (event `060d0483-50db-48d1-840b-73d9fc59356a`) has exactly 1 tier "Standard" at €500 with `tier_metadata.installments = {deposit_pct: 25, installments: [{ordinal:1, pct:50, days_after_booking:30}, {ordinal:2, pct:25, days_after_booking:60}]}`. Buyer `seth@somethingelsegroup.com` order `47374d23-2547-4709-a967-cee172fb877c` has `total_cents=12500`, `installment_plan_root=false`, `payment_status=paid`, zero rows in `order_installments`. Checkout session `60e8d83b-0d45-41c3-8f8a-80a9ffd5e54b` that produced this order HAS the full `installment_schedule` JSONB populated (`{fullPriceCents: 50000, depositCents: 12500, installments: [{ordinal:1, amountCents:25000, dueAt:2026-06-21}, {ordinal:2, amountCents:12500, dueAt:2026-07-21}]}`) and `status=paid_completed`. The session knew exactly what should have happened; the order didn't get the message. **Suspected root-cause candidates (PRE-INVESTIGATION, source-only reasoning):** (1) deposit PaymentIntent metadata key `mingla_installment_plan_root` not reaching the confirm/finalize RPC (Stripe webhook routing, metadata casing, or finalize RPC reading from the wrong field); (2) finalize RPC installments-INSERT branch silently no-oping when it can't find `installment_schedule` on the order JSON (cross-table read miss vs session schedule); (3) silent transaction abort after order INSERT but before installments INSERT; (4) finalize RPC reads `installment_schedule` from the wrong source. **Affected Surfaces:** buyer-anon-web (`/checkout-trip/{tripEventId}` — broken finalize), business-iOS + business-Android + business-web-preview (organiser sees false "Paid in full" + €0 outstanding on the post-ORCH-0914 Money tab). NOT in scope: consumer-iOS/Android (no trip-checkout flow), admin-web (no payment-plan ops surface yet). **Sequencing:** PROMOTES TO #1 PRIORITY ahead of S1 ORCH-0915 [Buyer pay-in-full opt-out] — ORCH-0915 was about giving buyers an OPT-OUT from forced installment plans, ORCH-0921 is about installment plans silently losing money even when intentionally chosen. **Pipeline next (sequential per operator one-step-at-a-time):** (a) operator confirms triage; (b) **HOT-FIX backfill** of the one known broken order via operator-gated SQL (INSERT 2 `order_installments` + flip `installment_plan_root=true` so existing cron picks up Jun 21 + Jul 21 charges automatically); (c) **AUDIT SELECT** across the whole DB to enumerate every order matching the leak pattern (`total_cents` equals deposit-amount of a tier's `tier_metadata.installments.deposit_pct` × full price AND `installment_plan_root=false` AND zero rows in `order_installments`) so we quantify the leak; (d) **INVESTIGATE+SPEC:** Claude `mingla-forensics` traces why finalize doesn't fire; (e) **IMPLEMENT** + DEPLOY + TEST + CLOSE per standard pipeline. **Hard guards:** preserve manual-charge-installment edge fn as manual recovery path; preserve cron ownership of off-session installment charges; fix MUST be idempotent + replayable for self-healing migrations; audit query MUST be read-only; backfill SQL is operator-only. > **2026-05-21 — ORCH-0903 [Consumer "how far" preference filter and displayed per-card travel-time disagree by up to ~30% — cards labeled 18–20 min appear when user sets 15-min cap] INTAKE REGISTERED — DISPATCH READY (Claude `mingla-forensics` INVESTIGATE).** Severity S2-medium (correctness / trust issue on the most heavily-used consumer-app filter — user sets an explicit travel-time cap and sees cards that visibly violate it; no crash, no data loss, but undermines the entire "how far" contract). Classification: `bug` + `ux` + `architecture-flaw` (the filter math and the display math are independent and disagree by design). Source: operator question 2026-05-21 ("how come when I put 15 min, 30 min, etc in how far on the preferences sheet, I still see cards that have travel times exceeding what I specified?"). **Plain-English impact:** today on the consumer-app preferences sheet, when a user picks "15 min" for "how far", the deck still surfaces cards labeled "18 min", "19 min", "20 min". The filter is NOT broken — it IS applied as a hard radius cut at the edge function. The mismatch is that the radius is computed with a 30% safety multiplier (`maxDistKm = (constraint/60) × speed × 1.3` at `supabase/functions/discover-cards/index.ts:729`) to compensate for the fact that haversine ≠ real road distance, but the per-card travel-time label shown to the user uses the same haversine/speed math WITHOUT the 1.3× compensation (`app-mobile/src/utils/travelTime.ts:23-34`). Net: a card at the radius edge passes the filter (haversine distance ≤ 13 km for a 15-min driving cap) but displays as `round(13/40 × 60) = 19.5 min`. Neither side calls Google Distance Matrix — both are speed-table guesses (driving=40 km/h, walking=4.5, etc.). **Root-cause options for SPEC to choose between:** (a) drop the 1.3× radius multiplier (under-restricts in dense urban areas where real road routes are 30%+ longer than straight-line — likely regresses real-world coverage); (b) **apply the 1.3× to the displayed estimate too** (display reads `round(distKm × 1.3 / speed × 60)` so user's "15 min" means "≤ 15 min route-adjusted estimate" everywhere — SPEC-recommended default); (c) cap displayed value at the user's setting (lies to user — REJECT); (d) call Google Distance Matrix for both filter and display (cost + latency hit — defer unless A/B shows large user-trust uplift); (e) hybrid: keep haversine for filter, call Distance Matrix only for the displayed value on visible cards (~6-12 cards at a time, batchable — cost-bounded). **Affected Surfaces:** consumer-iOS (primary — `app-mobile/` on iOS), consumer-Android (parity — shared RN code). Backend: `supabase/functions/discover-cards/` (radius math + per-card travel-time estimate). Surfaces explicitly NOT in scope: buyer-anon-web (no preferences sheet on anon checkout — buyers go straight to checkout from a known event/brand link), business-iOS / business-Android / business-web-preview (no consumer preferences sheet in the business app), admin-web (no consumer-side admin tooling for "how far"). **Hard guards for INVESTIGATE+SPEC:** (a) do NOT remove the 1.3× without proving real-route impact in a dense city sample (data, not vibes); (b) do NOT introduce Google Distance Matrix without operator cost-budget approval (Distance Matrix is metered per element — 12 visible cards × N preference-changes × M users compounds fast); (c) the chosen fix MUST keep filter and display in lockstep — whichever formula the filter uses, the display uses the same; (d) preserve solo/collab parity (the same fix must apply identically in `PreferencesSheet.tsx` solo path AND `board_session_preferences` collab path); (e) preserve append-only test contract per ORCH-0840 [Regression-test enforcement + append-only CI]; (f) regression-test gate Step 0.5 needs an implementor happy-path test asserting "all returned cards display travel time ≤ user constraint × tolerance" AND a tester adversarial test attacking edge cases (1-min constraint, 120-min constraint, walking mode, transit mode, anonymous user with no constraint set, zero-distance card). **Pipeline next:** Claude `mingla-forensics` INVESTIGATE mode against `Mingla_Artifacts/prompts/INVESTIGATOR_ORCH-0903_HOW_FAR_FILTER_DISPLAY_MISMATCH.md` (orchestrator-authored). Investigation MUST run on iOS sim + Android emulator (consumer app), capture screenshots of cards displaying values > user's constraint (proof of symptom), trace the radius formula end-to-end through `discover-cards` edge function + `query_servable_places_by_signal` RPC, prove the 1.3× hypothesis OR find a different root cause if applicable, and recommend ONE of the 5 option families above with quantitative evidence (sample dense-city haversine vs road-distance ratios from Google Maps web ground-truth on 5-10 reference routes). Sequential per operator one-step-at-a-time rule — INVESTIGATE returns → orchestrator REVIEW → SPEC → REVIEW → IMPLEMENT → TEST → CLOSE → EAS-OTA-publish. **EAS OTA status:** ELIGIBLE for option (b) — pure JS math change in `app-mobile/src/utils/travelTime.ts` + matching edge function deploy (no native, no migration). Options (d)/(e) require operator cost-budget approval and a new edge function call pattern. **Working tree:** `/Users/sethogieva/Desktop/mingla-main` on branch `Seth`. **Related:** ORCH-0904 [Consumer solo-deck location can be up to 5 min stale while user is moving] — same preferences flow, separate root cause, dispatched after ORCH-0903 CLOSE per sequential rule.

> **2026-05-21 — ORCH-0904 [Consumer solo-mode deck uses GPS location that can be up to 5 minutes stale — driving users filter against where they WERE, not where they ARE] INTAKE REGISTERED — PAUSED pending ORCH-0903 [How far filter/display mismatch] CLOSE (sequential per operator).** Severity S2-medium when user is mobile (driving scenario is the exact case the operator surfaced 2026-05-21); S3-low for stationary users. Classification: `bug` + `ux` + `architecture-flaw`. Source: operator question 2026-05-21 ("if I am driving and apply my preferences in the car, which location and travel time will be used?"). **Plain-English impact:** today the consumer-app solo-mode deck reads user location via the `useUserLocation` React Query hook with a 5-minute stale window (`app-mobile/src/hooks/useUserLocation.ts:155`). If the user applied preferences 3 minutes ago at point A and has driven 5 km to point B, the next deck fetch still uses point A's GPS — cards filter against where the user *was*, not where they *are*. Collab mode does NOT have this bug: it explicitly snapshots fresh GPS at the moment of "Apply" tap (`PreferencesSheet.tsx:862-866` calls `enhancedLocationService.getCurrentLocation()` synchronously and writes lat/lng to `board_session_preferences`). Solo mode skips that step and inherits whatever the React Query cache has. Custom-location users (`use_gps_location=false`) are unaffected — they always use their saved address. **Root-cause options for SPEC:** (a) **mirror collab path in solo** — `handleSavePreferences` calls `enhancedLocationService.getCurrentLocation()` synchronously when GPS mode is on, passes the fresh coords to the deck fetch via a `locationOverride` param (SPEC-recommended default — parity with collab, smallest blast radius); (b) drop `useUserLocation` staleTime to 30 seconds globally when `use_gps_location=true` AND app is foregrounded — refreshes deck more often as user moves (broader change, more GPS battery cost); (c) add a manual "Refresh location" tap on the deck so the user can re-anchor on demand (low-effort UX, but requires user to know the deck might be stale); (d) attach a "location captured X seconds ago" timestamp + visual indicator on the deck so the user can see staleness (transparency, not fix); (e) hybrid: option (a) for the preference-apply path + option (c) as a manual re-anchor affordance on the deck (recommended for full coverage). **Affected Surfaces:** consumer-iOS (primary), consumer-Android (parity). Surfaces explicitly NOT in scope: buyer-anon-web (no preferences sheet), business-iOS / business-Android / business-web-preview (no consumer deck in business app), admin-web (no consumer-side admin tooling). **Hard guards:** (a) do NOT drop staleTime globally without measuring battery impact (expo-location `getCurrentLocation` is not free — repeated foreground calls drain battery measurably); (b) do NOT introduce a background-location watcher (Apple/Google review-risk + battery + privacy — out of scope); (c) preserve the custom-location path entirely (`use_gps_location=false` users must continue to use their saved address; do NOT inject live GPS over a custom address); (d) the fresh-GPS call MUST have a timeout + fallback to last-known so a poor-GPS-fix scenario doesn't block the preferences apply (currently `enhancedLocationService` already implements this — verify and preserve); (e) preserve solo/collab parity per `feedback_solo_collab_parity.md` — whichever fix lands MUST apply to both modes consistently (collab already does the right thing; solo aligns up); (f) preserve append-only test contract per ORCH-0840 [Regression-test enforcement]. **Pipeline next:** PAUSED until ORCH-0903 CLOSE (sequential per operator). When unblocked: Claude `mingla-forensics` INVESTIGATE+SPEC (likely single-session — root cause already documented in this entry + ORCH-0903 investigation findings; INVESTIGATE confirms staleTime + traces hook usage on iOS sim, then SPEC). After SPEC → implementor → tester → CLOSE → EAS-OTA publish. **EAS OTA status:** ELIGIBLE — pure JS change (hook + service + preferences-apply path), no native, no migration, no edge function. **Working tree:** `/Users/sethogieva/Desktop/mingla-main` on branch `Seth`. **Related:** ORCH-0903 (sister bug surfaced in same operator question; share preferences-apply code path; ORCH-0903 lands first per sequential rule).

> **2026-05-12 - ORCH-0809 NEW - Discover Ticketmaster filter expansion v1: city picker + real segment/genre classification + local-time date window + remove broken price filter.** Type: missing-feature + design-debt + ux + invariant-violation (Constitution #3 No silent failures — price filter silently hides results with no UX signal; Constitution #9 No fabricated data — genre chips do keyword fuzzy-match and surface non-genre events as if they matched). Severity: S2 — corrodes Discover trust on the mobile app's primary content surface; not a launch blocker but a credibility hole. Surface: `app-mobile/` Discover screen + Ticketmaster Discovery API integration. Seed evidence (full audit performed in this session): location flow lives in `app-mobile/src/hooks/useUserLocation.ts:29-104` → `app-mobile/src/services/nightOutExperiencesService.ts:47-106` → `supabase/functions/ticketmaster-events/index.ts:309-322`; edge function sends only 8 of Ticketmaster Discovery API's 44 query parameters, with `segmentId` hardcoded to Music `KZFzniwnSyZfZ7v7nJ` at line 16 — Sports, Comedy, Arts & Theatre, Family, and Film events are unreachable from Discover. Genre filter at `app-mobile/src/screens/DiscoverScreen.tsx:1529-1559` does keyword fuzzy-match via `GENRE_TO_KEYWORDS` map at lines 102-114 — selecting "Hip-hop & R&B" can return jazz or unrelated events whose text happens to contain those words, and can miss real hip-hop events that don't spell the keyword out. Price filter at `DiscoverScreen.tsx:1086-1118` + 1497-1527 is pure client-side post-fetch hiding — Ticketmaster's Discovery API has no price query parameter, so the filter silently throws away results after fetch with zero UX signal (user sees an empty Discover and thinks there are no events nearby when really 30 events were filtered out). Date chips at `DiscoverScreen.tsx:1249-1282` pass UTC `startDateTime`/`endDateTime` instead of `localStartEndDateTime`, causing tonight/weekend/next-week/this-month to drift across timezones (e.g. at 10 PM PST on Friday, "This Weekend" already counts Friday as gone because UTC has rolled to Saturday). Radius is hardcoded to 50 km in two places (`nightOutExperiencesService.ts:66` and `ticketmaster-events/index.ts:269`) with no unit toggle. **Scope (locked by operator 2026-05-12):** (1) replace GPS-driven `latlong`+`radius` as primary location with a top-of-Discover user-editable city picker that defaults to the user's GPS-resolved city, persists the chosen city in `UserPreferences`, and drives the TM query via `city`+`stateCode`+`countryCode` (falls back to `latlong`+`radius` only when city resolves to fewer than 5 results); (2) replace hardcoded `segmentId=Music` with a multi-segment selector (Music, Sports, Arts & Theatre, Comedy, Family, Film) and replace keyword-based genre chips with a server-owned `genreId`/`subGenreId` map so chips pass real Ticketmaster classification IDs; (3) replace `startDateTime`/`endDateTime` with `localStartEndDateTime` so all four date chips (Tonight, This Weekend, Next Week, This Month) reflect the user's local clock; (4) remove the price filter entirely from Discover for Ticketmaster events — Ticketmaster has no structured price query, the client-side filter is dishonest, and the price-filter capability returns as a separate ORCH when Mingla Business native events (which have structured pricing via `ticketCheckout` flow) are integrated into Discover. **Out of scope (deferred to future ORCHs):** city picker affecting Mingla-native events or places; `marketId`/`dmaId` location parameters; `includeTBA`/`includeTBD` hygiene flags; `unit=miles` vs `km` toggle; sort options beyond `date,asc`; attraction/venue/promoter deep links; radius slider UI; reintroducing price filter (separate ORCH when Mingla Business events are wired into Discover). Required next lifecycle: skip INVESTIGATE (today's audit + Ticketmaster Discovery API parameter enumeration is the investigation in substance) → dispatch Claude `mingla-forensics` SPEC mode with `prompts/FORENSICS_ORCH-0809_DISCOVER_TICKETMASTER_FILTER_EXPANSION_V1.md`; expected output `specs/SPEC_ORCH-0809_DISCOVER_TICKETMASTER_FILTER_EXPANSION_V1.md`. Hard guard: no implementation, no edge-function schema change, no `UserPreferences` migration draft, no Ticketmaster classification ID enumeration before SPEC; spec must define edge-function request schema v2 as additive-and-backward-compatible, define cache-key schema migration, define city-autocomplete data source (Google Places Autocomplete already wired via `geocodingService`), and define failure modes (zero-result city, ambiguous city, GPS-never-resolved, user with no saved city, fallback trigger threshold).

> **2026-05-12 - ORCH-0793 CLOSED PASS - `biz_ticket_scan` time-window enforcement live end-to-end.** Plain-English impact: the scanner now refuses ticket scans that fall outside the event window (configurable grace: 120 min before start, 360 min after end). A buyer who accidentally scans a future-dated ticket today no longer permanently burns it — the RPC returns `not_yet_open` with the door time, the mobile UI shows an amber "Doors aren't open yet — Opens at 9:00 PM" overlay with warning haptic, and `tickets.status` stays `valid` so the same ticket succeeds when scanned within the window. Symmetric path for late scans: `event_ended` with relative-past formatting. Multi-day events succeed if `now()` is inside ANY of the event's `event_dates` rows (most-permissive policy). Legacy events with no `event_dates` fall through to existing success behavior (backward compat). Existing checks for `duplicate`, `wrong_event`, `void`, `not_found`, `scanner_not_authorized` unchanged. **Status:** CLOSED Grade A. **QA verdict:** TARGETED FAIL → REWORK → RETEST PASS — P0:0 / P1:0 / P2:0 / P3:0 / P4:1 (no IN_WINDOW or multi-date production fixtures available today; deferred to next real active event). **Two migrations shipped within the same close cycle** because tester live-fire caught a pre-existing `scan_events.scan_result` CHECK that v1 didn't widen — every out-of-window scan would have been rolled back by `check_violation` SQLSTATE 23514 and the user would have seen a generic red "Scan failed" overlay instead of the new "Doors aren't open yet" overlay. Fix (v2) is a one-line ALTER TABLE follow-up plus a new strict-grep Check 8 that fails CI for any future migration introducing a new `scan_result` value without widening the CHECK in the same PR (verified by negative control). **Invariant promoted DRAFT→ACTIVE:** I-PROPOSED-BB SCAN_TIME_WINDOW_ENFORCED — every `result='success'` MUST be the consequence of an `event_dates` window check (or the legacy no-event_dates fallback); out-of-window discriminators MUST NOT flip `tickets.status`; CHECK constraint MUST include both new values. Reinforces I-PROPOSED-AY EVENT_DATES_SOLE_DATE_AUTHORITY. **Migrations:** `20260528000000_orch_0793_scan_time_window.sql` + `20260528000001_orch_0793_widen_scan_result_check.sql` — both applied to remote (confirmed via `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`); both contain in-migration `DO $$` RAISE EXCEPTION verification probes. **Edge deploys:** none — `supabase/functions/scan-ticket/index.ts` source unchanged (transparent passthrough verified). **EAS OTA:** N/A — DB-only change; RPC lives on the server; mobile bundle picks up new behavior immediately via existing edge function. **DIAG reap:** zero `[ORCH-0793-DIAG]` markers (no diagnostic markers were placed during the cycle). **Discoveries:** D-0793-1 `events.status` auto-advance gap remains open (candidate ORCH-0794, P3); D-0793-2 ticket-type-level scan windows (future ORCH if product asks); D-0793-5 buyer-scan notification (defense-in-depth, deferred). **Process discovery:** SPEC + INVESTIGATION pass missed checking downstream CHECK constraints when introducing new enum values — codified as forensic checklist rule "for every new enum value an RPC emits, grep every CHECK constraint downstream." Strict-grep Check 8 now enforces the same rule at CI time for `scan_result` specifically. **Evidence:** investigation `reports/INVESTIGATION_ORCH-0793_BIZ_TICKET_SCAN_TIME_WINDOW.md`, spec `specs/SPEC_ORCH-0793_BIZ_TICKET_SCAN_TIME_WINDOW.md`, implementation v1 `reports/IMPLEMENTATION_ORCH-0793_BIZ_TICKET_SCAN_TIME_WINDOW_REPORT.md`, implementation v2 `reports/IMPLEMENTATION_ORCH-0793_BIZ_TICKET_SCAN_TIME_WINDOW_REPORT_v2.md`, v1 QA `reports/QA_ORCH-0793_BIZ_TICKET_SCAN_TIME_WINDOW_REPORT.md`, retest QA `reports/QA_ORCH-0793_BIZ_TICKET_SCAN_TIME_WINDOW_REPORT_RETEST_1.md`.

> **2026-05-11 - ORCH-0792 REGISTERED - Events created without `event_dates` rows silently collapse date-dependent rendering (calendar block, PDF date line, email date line, future .ics attachment).** Plain-English impact: an organiser can create and publish an event, sell paid tickets through real Stripe Checkout, and have the system accept the order — but if no `event_dates` row was written when the event was saved, the buyer's branded confirmation email loses the Add-to-Calendar block, the date line on the body, the date line on the ticket PDF, and any future `.ics` attachment, because every renderer defensively skips date output when `event.startAt = null`. Out of scope: branded email rendering (ORCH-0785 — defensive null handling is correct as-is), refund/cancel dispatcher (ORCH-0788), sender BIMI avatar (will be a separate ORCH).

> **2026-05-02 — ORCH-0708 NEW (S1) — Wave 2 Phase 1 photo-aesthetic scoring integration. Forensics + spec landed. Awaits implementor dispatch.** First Wave 2 deliverable. Auditable evidence from live Mingla-dev DB proves 5 structural limits in current scoring: (R-1) cap=200 squashes 5–7% of dining places at top — 2,620 places stuck at exactly 200 across casual_food / brunch / drinks / icebreakers; (R-2) popularity dominates 38–74% of every top-decile score, drowning quality differentiation; (R-3) text-pattern matching only fires for 3.6% of fine_dining places — 96.4% of the 50-point text budget is wasted; (R-4) NULL Google booleans devastate stale cities (London/Brussels/Baltimore = 100% NULL on serves_dinner/reservable/dine_in/wine/generative_summary; even DC/Raleigh/Cary/Durham/FL = 53–73% NULL); (R-5) per-city quality drift confirms ORCH-0702 (Baltimore p90 fine_dining=61.4 vs FL p90=109.7) — global filter_min is structurally wrong. **Architectural fix:** new `place_pool.photo_aesthetic_data jsonb` column owned EXCLUSIVELY by new `score-place-photo-aesthetics` edge function; 7 new JSONB-aware field-weight prefix matchers (`photo_aesthetic_above_X`, `photo_lighting_X`, `photo_composition_X`, `photo_subject_X`, `photo_vibe_includes_X`, `photo_appropriate_for_includes_X`, `photo_inappropriate_for_includes_X`, `photo_safety_includes_X`) extend signalScorer.ts (~70 LOC); 7 v_next signal config migrations adding photo-derived weights + raising cap 200→1000 on fine_dining, brunch, romantic, lively, casual_food, drinks, icebreakers; cap stays at 200 on the other 9 signals. **Asymmetric weight design** (§19 of spec) — photo data captured ONCE per place via Claude Haiku 4.5 vision call, scored DIFFERENTLY per signal. Same JSONB blob produces +170 in fine_dining and -100 in icebreakers for an upscale candle-lit place. Bidirectional misclassification fix (corrects false positives AND false negatives, including the Baltimore-NULL-boolean famine and the Trapeze-class promiscuity). **Cost:** ~$11 for Raleigh+Cary+Durham (3,234 places) at Haiku batch+cache, well under $200 escalation. **Prompt safeguards (7 layers, §20):** calibration examples baked in system prompt (6 anchored cases A–F covering upscale/brunch/dive/strip-club/storefront/coffeeshop) · anti-hedging rule · honest-grading rule · inappropriate_for discipline rule · `dry_run_sample` action for 30-place pre-flight at $0.10 per iter · 10 golden test fixtures (§22) · disagreement logging via new `photo_aesthetic_unknown_outputs` table. **Sonnet 4.6 escalation hatch (§21, optional flag)** for safety-flagged low-confidence places. **2 new invariants queued for CLOSE:** I-PHOTO-AESTHETIC-DATA-SOLE-OWNER + I-PHOTO-AESTHETIC-CACHE-FINGERPRINT (sha256 of stored_photo_urls.slice(0,5) drives idempotent skip on re-run). **Architectural constraint locked:** lives INSIDE current scoring system per `memory/project_place_intelligence_architecture.md`; NOT a replacement. Operator's stated UX target met: after deploy, "just run scoring again" works (one curl per signal). **6 discoveries:** D-INV-1 per-city percentile (Option C from cap decision) → ORCH-0709 candidate · D-INV-2 filter_min re-tune review during CLOSE · D-INV-3 unknown vibe_tags log table (folded into spec §20.7) · D-INV-4 London/Brussels/Lagos/Baltimore need admin-refresh-places (parallel ORCH item) · D-INV-5 AI columns still in schema despite memory-flagged decommission · D-INV-6 signal_definition_versions UNIQUE constraint still missing from ORCH-0702. **ID collision history:** ORCH-0704 → ORCH-0706 → ORCH-0708 (three collisions in one drafting session — pattern lesson for future orchestrator sessions: re-grep the ORCH counter at the top of every registration step, not just at SPEC drafting). **Files:** [reports/INVESTIGATION_ORCH-0708_SCORING_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md](reports/INVESTIGATION_ORCH-0708_SCORING_SYSTEM_AUDIT.md) · [reports/SPEC_ORCH-0708_PHOTO_AESTHETIC_SCORING_INTEGRATION.md](reports/SPEC_ORCH-0708_PHOTO_AESTHETIC_SCORING_INTEGRATION.md) · prompts/FORENSICS_ORCH-0708_PHOTO_AESTHETIC_SCORING_AUDIT_AND_SPEC.md (PRIVATE_PROMPT_NOT_VERSIONED: `Mingla_Artifacts/prompts/FORENSICS_ORCH-0708_PHOTO_AESTHETIC_SCORING_AUDIT_AND_SPEC.md`). **Status:** REVIEW APPROVED 10/10 · IMPL dispatch ready · awaits operator `/mingla-implementor` invocation. **Active queue post-this-entry:** ORCH-0708 IMPL dispatch ready (operator runs `/mingla-implementor`); ORCH-0709 (per-city percentile) deferred to Wave 2 follow-up cycle after ORCH-0708 ships; ORCH-0700 SPEC v2 still blocked on operator decisions; PR #59 ORCH-0706 + ORCH-0707 in their own queues.

## User Journey

### Phase 1: Acquisition
Install → Welcome Screen → OAuth (Google/Apple)

### Phase 2: Onboarding
Phone OTP → Gender → Details → Value Prop → Intent → Location → Preferences → Friends → Collab → Consent → Deck Ready

### Phase 3: Core Loop
Explore (deck swipe) → Save → Schedule → Invite → Collaborate → Go → Review

### Phase 4: Retention
Calendar reminders → Push notifications → Holiday experiences → Re-engagement → Subscription upgrade

### Phase 5: Social
Friend discovery → Pair requests → DM → Map presence → Activity feed

> **2026-05-24 — ORCH-0951 [Multi-ticket QR carousel host has zero width on first paint — pageWidth chicken-and-egg] CLOSED PASS / hotfix.** S1-high / `bug` + `regression`. Affected Surfaces: buyer-anonymous web ONLY (`mingla-business` `/checkout-trip/{tripEventId}/confirm` and `/checkout/{eventId}/confirm` — the post-Stripe-redirect confirm pages where the multi-ticket carousel mounts). Surfaces explicitly NOT in scope: consumer iOS/Android (no carousel), business iOS/Android (separate native app, no buyer-web), admin-web (no checkout). **Bug:** `TicketQrCarousel.tsx`'s multi-ticket render path has an `if (pageWidth === 0) return <View style={styles.host} onLayout={handleLayout} />` early-return (ORCH-0852-era). The empty bare host inherits `alignSelf: "stretch"` from `styles.host` but mounts inside a parent (`qrCard`) with `alignItems: "center"` — on RNW the empty View collapses to ~0 width because no children define its width and the center-aligned parent doesn't stretch it. `onLayout` fires with width=0 → `pageWidth` stays 0 → early-return loops forever → only the bare empty host with `minHeight: 320` renders → user sees a thin vertical strip with no QR codes. Single-ticket case unaffected (uses `styles.singleWrap` which has no `alignSelf: "stretch"` and sizes to its child QR image). **Why it surfaced now:** ORCH-0852 introduced the early-return; previous broken hydration paths (#418 and the ORCH-0930 attempts) prevented us from getting this far for multi-ticket renders on web. ORCH-0932's server-side QR PNG fix made the rest of the pipeline work, exposing the latent layout bug. **Fix:** add `width: "100%"` to `styles.host` so the empty bare host has a definite width on first paint regardless of parent alignment. One line in `mingla-business/src/components/checkout/TicketQrCarousel.tsx`. Native ignores `width: "100%"` when no width constraint is present — behavior identical to pre-fix on iOS/Android. **Regression tests:** implementor happy-path asserts `styles.host` declares `width: "100%"`; tester adversarial asserts the `pageWidth === 0` early-return path is preserved (defense against future "simplification" that would break native by removing the gate entirely). Both at `mingla-business/src/components/checkout/__tests__/orch_0951_carousel_host_width.test.tsx`. **Live-fire evidence (operator screenshot 2026-05-24):** order `d99081c3-c77d-462e-a0ff-1e0345222af5` (3× DC Adventure Standard, paid €375 deposit) — DB confirms 3 valid tickets with qr_code populated; buyer-web carousel renders only the thin strip; no QR codes visible. **Pipeline:** INVESTIGATE → IMPLEMENT → TEST → CLOSE all in this session as a hotfix (1-line fix; full-fidelity diagnosis from screenshot + DB probe + source trace). Working tree: `/Users/sethogieva/Desktop/mingla-main` on branch `Seth`.

Surfaces explicitly NOT in scope: consumer iOS / consumer Android (consumer app does not edit business trips), admin-web (no trip capacity editing). **The bug:** trip-capacity has two storage locations — `events.theme -> 'business_trip' -> 'capacity'` (JSONB blob) and `ticket_types.quantity_total` (integer column). Mechanism: on a MIXED deck (≥1 category + ≥1 curated pill), `onSinglesReady` in `useDeckCards.ts:148-162` writes `setQueryData(singles)` when singles resolve (~1s) → UI renders singles-only. User may start swiping. Later, full `fetchDeck` promise resolves with 1:1 interleaved `regular+curated` at `deckService.ts:484-503` — positions 0,1,2,3,4 become `reg[0], cur[0], reg[1], cur[1], reg[2]` instead of `reg[0..4]`. React Query overwrites cache. `recommendations` state changes. `SwipeableCards.tsx:979-980` sees first-5-IDs differ → WIPE #2: `setRemovedCards(new Set()) + setCurrentCardIndex(0)`. Any swipes in the singles-only window are lost. Occurs on EVERY solo user with curated pills on EVERY pref change. Confidence: H on mechanism (code-proven), M on user-visible outcome (depends on swipe timing; device test would confirm). Shares fix with ORCH-0491 + ORCH-0493 RC#1 (narrow "deck expanded, same session" signal vs full-replacement signal). Absorb into ORCH-0490 Phase 2.3 or dedicated slice — spec-writer call. |

Fix directions: prune entries not matching current `deckPrefsHash` on hydration, OR scope the persister to a single active key. Defer to post-ORCH-0490 unless the 1.5MB cap is hit in beta testing. |

Post-rework timing on Mingla-dev: **3,061ms warm** (down from 5,118ms pre-rework). Under PostgREST 8s timeout so the admin country-drill-down page loads, but 6× over the <500ms spec target. Root cause: Bitmap Heap Scan on 4,858 MV heap pages for a single country's ~31k rows (columns `has_photos`, `primary_category`, `rating`, `city_id` are not in the existing `(country_code, is_active, ai_approved)` index, forcing heap access for projection). | ORCH-0488 | Admin RPC cache-sensitivity on Mingla-dev — 2-5s cold-cache latencies across multiple admin_* RPCs (not just city_overview) | Admin + Backend | S2 | performance | open | F | — | Registered 2026-04-17 from ORCH-0481 tester cycle 1 retest D-NEW-6. Tester observed: `admin_place_country_overview` 87ms hot / 5,047ms mildly-cold / 6,832ms fully-cold; `admin_place_category_breakdown` 107ms cycle 0 / 4,219ms cycle 1 (unchanged body — plan drift + cold cache). Root cause: Mingla-dev's slow I/O (~1ms per heap page read) means the 44MB MV (27 cols × 63k rows) exceeds shared_buffers working set. When pages get evicted between queries, re-reads are I/O-bound. **Decision point: is this Mingla-dev-only or does it replicate on production?** Production may have larger shared_buffers / faster disk → cache hit ratios closer to 100% → sub-500ms consistently. **Defer evaluation until post-production deploy.** If prod also sees 2-5s latencies, the structural fix is to narrow the MV (drop TOAST'd columns like `stored_photo_urls raw`, `photos jsonb`, `ai_categories raw`, `types raw` that only a few RPCs need — reduces physical footprint ~10× to 4-5MB, fits in cache). Not blocking close if admin page loads under 8s. |

| ORCH-0872 | Tr3 Installment Payments Stage 1c — plumb the 3 new finalize params through the SECONDARY finalize callers. ORCH-0869 [Tr3 Installment Payments] Stage 1b updated the PRIMARY caller `supabase/functions/_shared/stripeWebhookRouter.ts:763-797` to extract `paymentIntent.customer` + `paymentIntent.payment_method` from a deposit PI whose metadata carries `mingla_installment_plan_root='true'` and pass them through to the new 8-arg `biz_ticket_checkout_finalize` RPC. Two SECONDARY callers still pass 5 params and let the 3 new ones default: `supabase/functions/reconcile-stuck-checkouts/index.ts:74-83` (stuck-session recovery) and `supabase/functions/ticket-checkout-confirm/index.ts:263-272` (alternative confirm path). For non-installment recoveries this is byte-safe (the params default null/null/false → legacy behaviour). **The hole:** if a real installment-plan deposit PI succeeds but the Stripe webhook crashes or never arrives (rare — webhook is authoritative), the buyer would later trigger reconcile or confirm, an order would be created WITHOUT `order_installments` rows + null customer/PM columns, and the cron would have nothing to schedule. Buyer pays deposit, trip stays in "paid" status without future commitments, planner's Money tab shows no scheduled installments, manual operator recovery via direct SQL only. Scope: surgical 6-line additions per caller mirroring `stripeWebhookRouter.ts` extraction pattern + 1 adversarial source-assertion test per caller. | ORCH-0884 | **IntakeTypePickerSheet height + sibling-Modal race** — two Phase 3 regressions in the intake type-picker UX surfaced post-ORCH-0880 [Tr5 Traveler Intake Forms] merge by operator live-fire on iPhone. **Bug A (sibling-Modal race, S1):** in `IntakeSchemaBuilder.handleTypePickerSelect` the picker close (`setTypePickerOpen(false)`) AND editor mount (`setEditorState({ visible: true, ... })`) fire synchronously back-to-back. Sheet primitive keeps the Modal mounted for `UNMOUNT_DELAY_MS=280ms` after `visible=false` to play the close animation, so for ~280ms both Modals are mounted at the OS root layer simultaneously. RN's native Modal can only foreground one at a time — the newer (Editor) Modal gets visually blocked by the older (Picker) Modal still animating closed → app appears frozen → buyer never sees the editor → cannot add ANY question type. Pattern explicitly warned against by `feedback_rn_sub_sheet_must_render_inside_parent.md` ("Native Modal sibling-mounts compete at the OS root layer; the second one mounted gets visually blocked"). The Phase 3 implementor's inline comment at IntakeSchemaBuilder.tsx:448-449 cites the memory but applied it INCORRECTLY — Editor is rendered as a sibling of the picker, not nested inside. **Bug B (height clipping, S1):** `IntakeTypePickerSheet` numeric `snapPoint = 520` measured short of actual content height (~556pt: 4 rows × 110pt cards + 3 × 8pt gaps + ~50pt header + ~14pt drag handle + ~28pt body padding). On iPhone 17 Pro the 36pt overflow clipped the File upload card's bottom half off-screen — file_upload question type unreachable from the picker. **Operator verified live on iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.4 dev build post-ORCH-0880 EAS build install via screenshot.** **Fix A:** wrap `setEditorState` in `setTimeout(..., 300)` (> UNMOUNT_DELAY_MS=280) inside handleTypePickerSelect so picker Modal fully unmounts before editor Modal mounts. **Fix B:** bump TYPE_PICKER_SHEET_HEIGHT 520→640 (≥600 safety floor, 84pt headroom) + wrap grid in `<ScrollView>` for defense-in-depth on small devices (iPhone SE where 640pt exceeds 95% screen clamp). **Affected Surfaces:** business-iOS + business-Android + business-web-preview (planner Step 6 wizard schema-builder + EditPublishedTripScreen Intake form accordion both consume IntakeSchemaBuilder which mounts both sheets). **Surfaces NOT in scope:** consumer-iOS/Android (no trip wizard); admin-web (no trip wizard); buyer-anon-web (buyer-fill route uses different IntakeFormRenderer + IntakeFilePickerChooserSheet, NOT IntakeTypePickerSheet — buyer-anon path unaffected); database (no schema change); edge functions (no backend change). **Severity = S1-high** because the intake type picker is the ONLY entry point to add intake questions; both bugs together make the entire intake-form-authoring feature unusable on real iPhone hardware. **Hotfix bundle justified** per one-PR-per-CLOSE narrow exception (tightly-coupled hotfix convoy): both fixes in the same component family (IntakeSchemaBuilder + IntakeTypePickerSheet), same root cause family (Phase 3 oversights), same regression cause, same OTA-eligible scope, same test file. Bundling avoids 2-PR convoy + minimizes operator burden. **EAS OTA eligible: YES** (pure JS — no native module added; layout constant + ScrollView wrap + setTimeout pattern). **Hard guards inherited:** ORCH-0880 6 I-PROPOSED-TR5-* invariants (unchanged); `feedback_rn_sub_sheet_must_render_inside_parent.md` (now correctly applied via setTimeout deferral pattern); `feedback_rn_color_formats.md`; `feedback_toast_needs_absolute_wrap.md`; `feedback_keyboard_never_blocks_input.md`; Constitution #3 (no silent failures — Fix A surfaces the editor); Constitution #1 (no dead taps — Fix B makes file_upload card reachable); I-38 + I-39 (touch + a11y unchanged). **Regression test:** `mingla-business/src/components/trip/__tests__/IntakeTypePickerSheet_orch_0884_regression.test.ts` — 3 tests (Fix A setTimeout pattern present + delay >=280ms; Fix B height >=600; Fix B ScrollView wrap present). | ORCH-0877 | **Event end-time display + midnight-crossing single-day authoring** — two coupled gaps in how the Mingla event-time window is rendered and authored across every surface that touches `event_dates`. **S-1 (display, bug, S1):** every event-display surface in Mingla shows only the start time (`event_dates.start_at` rendered as a human string) and silently drops the end time (`event_dates.end_at`) even though the column exists and is populated by the publish RPCs (ORCH-0792/0824). Confirmed at schema layer: `event_dates_end_after_start` CHECK constraint enforces `end_at > start_at`, so the data IS authoritative. The display selectors / formatters / templates strip it. Affected display surfaces (forensics will harden — preliminary): consumer-iOS/Android event detail + event cards + feed cards + ticket-confirmation screens + push notification copy + calendar add-to-cal integrations; buyer-anon web `/e/{brandSlug}/{eventSlug}` + `/checkout/{eventId}/{buyer,payment,confirm}`; business-iOS/Android + business-web-preview event detail + EditPublishedScreen When section + brand-side preview tiles; admin-web event admin views; email templates in `supabase/functions/_shared/email/*` (ticket confirmation + reminder + marketing); OneSignal push payloads; `events_with_master_date` matview consumers. **S-2 (authoring, missing-feature, S1):** event creator on mingla-business (EventCreatorWizard Step 2 "When/Where") presumably constrains the end-time picker to the same calendar day as start-time, so a real single-occurrence event like "Saturday 10pm → Sunday 2am" cannot be authored as ONE event. Operator currently must either author an incorrect end (10pm → 11:59pm), author a "multi-day" event (wrong shape — two date rows, two ticket scans), or skip end-time entirely. Forensics must prove (a) where the same-day constraint lives (picker UI, validation layer, RPC, or DB), (b) whether `event_dates.start_at` + `end_at` already correctly persist a cross-midnight value when the constraint is bypassed, (c) the right UX for "ends next day" (explicit "ends next day" toggle, free date+time picker per field, smart inference when end-hour < start-hour, etc.), (d) whether published-event edit (EditPublishedScreen "When" section) has the same constraint and needs the same fix. **Why these two MUST ship together (coupling proven at INTAKE):** if we fix display only, we start rendering end-times that are wrong for midnight-crossing events because the authoring UX never produced a correct `end_at` for them; if we fix authoring only, the new correct `end_at` values are invisible everywhere users could see them. One ORCH, one PR, one regression net. **Operator-locked at INTAKE 2026-05-18 (operator confirmed scope via AskUserQuestion = "Yes — proceed to dispatch"):** (a) both sub-symptoms in ONE ORCH-0877 (tightly coupled by data + UX); preserve every existing event display contract for events that DON'T cross midnight. **Hard guards (mandatory in SPEC):** preserve current display for events where `end_at` falls on the SAME calendar day as `start_at` (do not regress the 99% case);
